en: The Hymn for Deliverance from Hell:
Sunk in the mire of poverty within the great ocean called saṃsāra, I call upon you, O Tathāgata, who made a vow at the time of your birth: "Protect me indeed! (1)
O Tathāgata, protect me, who am lying in the house of darkness, experiencing misfortune and suffering, and abandoned by my circle of kinsmen.
Mother, father, sisters, and so forth, as well as sons, wives, and friends—these are seen to be like a magical illusion; therefore, O Tathāgata, protect me!
For the sake of my enemies, I have committed both good and evil deeds;
I alone shall surely experience their fruit—save me, O Tathāgata!
O Lord, O Tathāgata, I have become blinded in this most terrible, unfathomable ocean of a ruined well; indeed, protect me!
Mounted upon a dilapidated boat for the crossing of the great ocean, I have seen that which is difficult to cross; O Tathāgata, indeed protect me!
Dharma and adharma were not understood by me, nor was the distinction between what is approachable and what is unapproachable known.
O Protector, I am devoid of consciousness; therefore, O Tathāgata, save me! (7)
I have committed the five acts of immediate retribution, such as matricide;
I am being cooked in a terrible hell—save me, O Tathāgata! (8)
I have caused the destruction of stūpas and ruined the affairs of the Saṅgha;
I have committed violence against sentient beings—save me, O Tathāgata!
Deprived of happiness in this world and feeling no sensation in the next world, bound by the thread of karma—save me indeed, O Tathāgata! 10.
Just as a kāśa flower is tossed about in the sky by the wind, such is life in this world; O Tathāgata, protect me! 11.
The forest is overgrown with thorns and crowded with many trees;
I do not see a path here—save me, O Tathāgata! (12)
"Innocent deer were slain by me in my anger at an improper time;
therefore, O Tathāgata, I consider myself guilty of regicide—save me! (13)
As I am being cooked in hell, will there be anyone to save me?
To whom shall I go for refuge? O Tathāgata, please protect me! 14.
Among physicians, you are the King of Physicians, the healer of all diseases;
O Lord of the World, you are the protector of the world within the three realms, including all that is mobile and immobile. 15.
The *Narakoddhāra-stotra* is completed.
